title: ok26jr
Fadak and Lady Fatima's Estrangement
hook: Fadak, which the Prophet had given to his daughter, was taken from her hand. She stated her right through a verse and died estranged.
scenes.0.text: While the pledge of allegiance was being taken at Saqifa, **Imam Ali** was in Medina, at the Prophet's funeral. Bay'a is a pledge of allegiance. After that came the matter of **Fadak**. **Fadak** was a village north of Medina, near Khaybar. Its people had come to terms without drawing a sword. The Prophet had given this palm grove as a hiba to his daughter, **Lady Fatima**. Hiba means gift. The income of **Fadak** covered a large part of the livelihood of the ==Ahl al-Bayt==.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.1.text: In Medina, the Prophet had only just died. The grief had not yet subsided. **Caliph Abu Bakr** seized **Fadak** from **Lady Fatima**'s hand. In the Shia reading, the grove was taken so that the ==Ahl al-Bayt== would not grow strong through its income and **Imam Ali** could not defend his right with it. **Lady Fatima** could not keep her father's gift in her hand.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.2.text: After the seizure, **Lady Fatima** went out to the Mosque of Medina. She delivered the **Fadak** sermon. She was grieved because her father's gift had been taken from her hand. She stated her right openly. The congregation heard her. The saying set against her was this: "We prophets do not leave inheritance. What we leave is charity." **Lady Fatima** answered this saying with the Qur'an. **Solomon** had inherited from **David**. **Yahya** had inherited from **Zechariah**. Neml 16 and Meryem 6 did not deny the inheritance of the children of prophets. **Lady Fatima** defended her right with these verses.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.3.text: After the sermon, **Lady Fatima** brought witnesses in Medina. One was her husband **Imam Ali**. One was **Umm Ayman**. **Umm Ayman** was a woman who had grown up in the Prophet's house and knew his affection closely. Both said that **Fadak** had been given as a hiba to **Lady Fatima**. The testimony was not accepted. **Lady Fatima**, in whose hand the property was, was asked for documents. The word of **Imam Ali** and **Umm Ayman** was rejected. The ==Ahl al-Bayt== were not listened to in a matter of their own house.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.art.actors.2.label: 19dj5z1
Umm Ayman
scenes.4.text: The Prophet had said of his daughter **Lady Fatima**: "Fatima is a part of me. Whoever angers her has angered me." When the witnesses were rejected, **Lady Fatima** became estranged from **Caliph Abu Bakr** in Medina. She kept away from him. She did not speak to him until her death. This silence was not a whim. Her father's gift, the inheritance she defended with a verse, and the word of the witnesses had all been rejected at once. **Lady Fatima** kept up this hurt until she died.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 1kk5h3t
Lady Fatima
scenes.5.text: In Medina, **Lady Fatima** died estranged. The estrangement did not end here. **Imam Ali** washed her at night. He himself performed her prayer. He buried her in the dark. He did not inform **Caliph Abu Bakr**. **Imam Ali** preserved his wife's hurt up to the day of the burial. The front of the door, the days of illness, the night burial and the hidden grave are in the later story: **the Days of Fatima (Ayyam-i Fatimiyya)**.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: Centuries later, **Umar b. Abd al-Aziz** returned **Fadak** to **Lady Fatima**'s descendants. A later caliph took the same grove back again. **Lady Fatima**'s pain did not pass. The right of the ==Ahl al-Bayt== was the same palm grove both on the day it was given and on the day it was seized. Those who love them remember this palm grove as the last lawful property the Prophet left to his daughter.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: xt2qi8
Umar b. Abd al-Aziz
sunni.0.says: Lady Fatima asks Caliph Abu Bakr for her inheritance; she is refused; Lady Fatima becomes angry and remains estranged until she dies; Imam Ali buries her at night, does not inform Caliph Abu Bakr; Imam Ali later pledges allegiance.
sunni.1.says: Parallel narrations of the same event: the inheritance request and the answer "prophets do not leave inheritance."
sunni.2.says: Caliph Abu Bakr's narration about the Prophet's inheritance and Lady Fatima's request.
sunni.3.says: "Lady Fatima is a part of me; whoever angers her has angered me."
sunni.4.says: The return of Fadak to Lady Fatima's descendants by Umar b. Abd al-Aziz and al-Ma'mun.
shia.0.says: The gift of Fadak to Lady Fatima as a hiba, and the witnesses.
shia.0.grade: The page was not reopened in this round. Reading the seizure as stemming from fear over the caliphate is the Shia school's interpretation of this usurpation. A separate page number was not given.
shia.1.says: The Fadak sermon that Lady Fatima delivered in the mosque. Neml 16 and Meryem 6, as the answer to the inheritance of the children of prophets, are in the Shia reading of this sermon.
shia.2.says: The tensions in the process of the pledge of allegiance.
disputes.0.title: za2e8g
To whom did Fadak belong?
disputes.0.sunni: Fadak was land taken without war and was at the Prophet's disposal. In the Sunni reading, after the Prophet it is the state's charity.
disputes.0.shia: Fadak was land taken without war. In the Shia reading, the Prophet had given it to Lady Fatima as a hiba. The seizure is read as leaving the Ahl al-Bayt economically weak and cutting off the strength to defend Imam Ali's right to the caliphate.
disputes.1.title: qzb3z3
"Prophets do not leave inheritance"
disputes.1.sunni: The saying "Prophets do not leave inheritance" appears in Bukhari as a narration of Caliph Abu Bakr. In the Sunni reading, the hadith is sahih. The inheritance verses in the Qur'an are regarded as an inheritance of knowledge and prophethood.
disputes.1.shia: Lady Fatima sets Neml 16 and Meryem 6 against this saying: Solomon inherited from David, Yahya from Zechariah. Imam Ali and Umm Ayman were brought as witnesses, and their words were not accepted.
disputes.2.title: 1nvqs0p
Lady Fatima's estrangement
disputes.2.sunni: Bukhari 4240 reports that Lady Fatima remained estranged until her death and was buried at night.
disputes.2.shia: This estrangement combines with the taking of the gifted Fadak and the rejection of the sermon and the testimony. The saying "Whoever angers her has angered me" makes this pain the Prophet's pain.
questions.0: The Prophet had said, "Fatima is a part of me." Where does her standing in the mosque for Fadak keep love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: Imam Ali and Umm Ayman bore witness, and their words were not taken. How does it feel to ask documents of a woman in whose hand the property was?
questions.2: Lady Fatima died estranged. What does this silence tell you, as a right carried all the way to the grave?
summary: The Prophet had given Fadak to Lady Fatima as a hiba. Caliph Abu Bakr seized it. Lady Fatima answered in the mosque with Neml 16 and Meryem 6. The testimony of Imam Ali and Umm Ayman was not accepted. She died estranged. Bukhari 4240 records the estrangement and the night burial. The hiba and the witnesses are in the record of al-Kafi 1/543. The sermon is in Balaghat al-Nisa'. A page number was not given separately.
notes.0: Fadak was a village near Khaybar that came to terms without fighting and was at the Prophet's disposal.
notes.1: Lady Fatima asked Caliph Abu Bakr for Fadak and her share of the inheritance.
notes.2: Caliph Abu Bakr refused with the hadith «We prophets do not leave inheritance.»
notes.3: Lady Fatima became estranged over this and did not speak until her death (Bukhari 4240).
notes.4: Fadak was later returned by Umar b. Abd al-Aziz.
